title: Basic (built-in) data types
text: Python's main built-in types: numeric types int (arbitrary precision integers), float (double precision), complex (3+4j); bool (True/False, a subclass of int); text type str (immutable Unicode strings); sequence types list (mutable), tuple (immutable), range; binary types bytes, bytearray, memoryview; set types set (mutable) and frozenset (immutable); mapping type dict; and the special value None (type NoneType). Use type(x) or isinstance(x, int) to inspect types.

title: Lists
text: A list is an ordered, mutable sequence: nums = [1, 2, 3]. Common methods: append(x), extend(iterable), insert(i, x), remove(x), pop([i]), sort(), reverse(), index(x), count(x). Indexing nums[0], negative indexing nums[-1], slicing nums[1:3], nums[::-1]. len(nums) gives the length.

title: Tuples
text: A tuple is an ordered, immutable sequence: point = (3, 4). One-element tuple needs a comma: (5,). Tuples support unpacking: x, y = point. They can be dict keys if their items are hashable. collections.namedtuple and typing.NamedTuple give named fields.

title: Dictionaries
text: A dict maps hashable keys to values and keeps insertion order (Python 3.7+): ages = {'ann': 31, 'bob': 25}. Access ages['ann'], safe access ages.get('eve', 0), iterate with for k, v in ages.items(). Methods: keys(), values(), items(), update(), pop(), setdefault(). Dict comprehension: {x: x*x for x in range(5)}. Merge with a | b (3.9+).

title: Sets
text: A set is an unordered collection of unique hashable items: s = {1, 2, 3}; empty set is set() (not {}). Operations: union a | b, intersection a & b, difference a - b, symmetric difference a ^ b, membership x in s (fast, O(1) on average). frozenset is the immutable version.

title: Strings
text: str is an immutable sequence of Unicode characters. Literals: 'a', "b", '''multi-line'''. Useful methods: upper(), lower(), strip(), split(sep), sep.join(list), replace(a, b), startswith(), find(). Formatting: f-strings f'{name} is {age:.1f}', str.format(). Raw strings r'\n' keep backslashes.

title: Mutable vs immutable objects
text: Immutable types cannot be changed after creation: int, float, complex, bool, str, tuple, frozenset, bytes. Mutable types can be changed in place: list, dict, set, bytearray and most user-defined objects. Only hashable (usually immutable) objects can be dict keys or set members.

title: Variables and dynamic typing
text: Python is dynamically and strongly typed: variables are names bound to objects, the type belongs to the object, not the name. x = 5 then x = 'hi' is allowed. Assignment never copies; a = b makes both names refer to the same object. Use copy.copy / copy.deepcopy to copy.

title: Type hints
text: Type hints annotate expected types: def add(a: int, b: int) -> int. Collections: list[int], dict[str, float], tuple[int, ...]; optional values int | None (3.10+) or Optional[int]. Hints are not enforced at runtime; tools like mypy or pyright check them.

title: Functions
text: Define functions with def: def greet(name, greeting='Hello'): return f'{greeting}, {name}'. Arguments can be positional or keyword; *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple, **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a dict. Avoid mutable default values (use None). Functions are first-class objects.

title: Lambda functions
text: lambda creates a small anonymous function with a single expression: square = lambda x: x * x. Typical use is as a key function: sorted(people, key=lambda p: p.age). map(f, it) and filter(pred, it) also accept lambdas, though comprehensions are often clearer.

title: Classes and objects
text: Define classes with class: class Dog: def __init__(self, name): self.name = name; def bark(self): return 'Woof'. self refers to the instance. Inheritance: class Puppy(Dog): ... and super().__init__(...). Special (dunder) methods like __str__, __repr__, __eq__, __len__ customize behaviour. @classmethod, @staticmethod and @property are common decorators.

title: Dataclasses
text: from dataclasses import dataclass; @dataclass class Point: x: float; y: float = 0.0 automatically generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__. Options: frozen=True for immutability, order=True for comparisons, field(default_factory=list) for mutable defaults.

title: Control flow: if, for, while
text: if/elif/else choose branches; for x in iterable loops over items; while condition loops until false; break exits a loop, continue skips to the next iteration; loops may have an else block run when no break happened. range(start, stop, step) generates numbers. enumerate() gives index and item, zip() iterates in parallel. Python 3.10+ has structural pattern matching: match/case.

title: Comprehensions
text: List comprehension: [x * x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]. Also dict {k: v for ...}, set {x for ...} and generator expressions (x for x in ...) which are lazy. Nested: [(a, b) for a in A for b in B].

title: Exceptions and error handling
text: Handle errors with try/except: try: x = int(s) except ValueError as e: print(e) else: ... finally: .... raise ValueError('bad value') raises an exception. Create custom exceptions by subclassing Exception. Common built-ins: ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError, ZeroDivisionError, FileNotFoundError.

title: Files and context managers
text: Open files with a context manager so they close automatically: with open('data.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f: text = f.read(). Modes: 'r' read, 'w' write, 'a' append, 'b' binary. Iterate lines with for line in f. pathlib.Path offers Path('a.txt').read_text() and write_text().

title: Modules, packages and imports
text: A module is a .py file; a package is a directory of modules (usually with __init__.py). Import with import math, from math import sqrt, import numpy as np. Install third-party packages with pip install name, preferably inside a virtual environment: python -m venv .venv. if __name__ == '__main__': runs code only when the file is executed directly.

title: Iterators and generators
text: An iterator implements __iter__ and __next__. A generator function uses yield to produce values lazily: def count(n): i = 0; while i < n: yield i; i += 1. Generators save memory for large sequences. itertools provides tools like chain, islice, product, groupby.

title: Decorators
text: A decorator is a function that takes a function and returns a new one: def log(f): @functools.wraps(f) def wrapper(*a, **kw): print('call', f.__name__); return f(*a, **kw); return wrapper. Apply it with @log above a def. Built-in examples: @property, @staticmethod, @classmethod, @functools.lru_cache.

title: Operators
text: Arithmetic: + - * / (true division, gives float), // (floor division), % (modulo), ** (power). Comparison: == != < > <= >=, identity is / is not, membership in / not in. Logical: and, or, not. Bitwise: & | ^ ~ << >>. Walrus operator := assigns inside expressions (3.8+).

title: None and truthiness
text: None represents the absence of a value; compare with is None. Falsy values: None, False, 0, 0.0, '', [], {}, set(), range(0). Everything else is truthy, so if items: checks for a non-empty list.

title: Type conversion (casting)
text: Convert with the type constructors: int('42') -> 42, float('3.5') -> 3.5, str(10) -> '10', list('abc') -> ['a','b','c'], tuple([1,2]), set([1,1,2]) -> {1,2}, bool(0) -> False. int('abc') raises ValueError. int(3.9) truncates to 3; round(3.9) gives 4.

title: Async programming (asyncio)
text: async def defines a coroutine; await pauses it until another awaitable finishes. Run with asyncio.run(main()). asyncio.gather runs coroutines concurrently. Good for I/O-bound work (network, files); for CPU-bound work use multiprocessing.

title: Threads, processes and the GIL
text: threading runs threads that share memory; in CPython the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time, so threads help mostly with I/O-bound tasks. multiprocessing and concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor use separate processes for CPU-bound parallelism. Python 3.13 adds an optional free-threaded build.

title: Standard library highlights
text: Useful standard modules: os and pathlib (files), sys (interpreter), json (JSON), csv, datetime (dates/times), math and statistics, random, re (regular expressions), collections (Counter, defaultdict, deque, namedtuple), itertools, functools, logging, subprocess, unittest, sqlite3, http.server, argparse.

title: Virtual environments and pip
text: Create an isolated environment: python -m venv .venv, activate it (Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate, Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate), then pip install package. Save dependencies with pip freeze > requirements.txt and restore with pip install -r requirements.txt.

title: Scope: global, local, nonlocal
text: Names are resolved by the LEGB rule: Local, Enclosing, Global, Built-in. Assigning to a global inside a function requires the global statement; to an enclosing function variable requires nonlocal. Inner functions that capture outer variables are closures.

title: What is Python
text: Python is a high-level, interpreted, dynamically typed, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasizes readability (significant indentation) and has a huge standard library. The reference implementation is CPython; current versions are Python 3.x (Python 2 reached end of life in 2020).

title: Testing with unittest and pytest
text: unittest is built in: class TestMath(unittest.TestCase): def test_add(self): self.assertEqual(1 + 1, 2). pytest is a popular third-party tool where plain functions with assert work: def test_add(): assert add(1, 2) == 3; run with pytest.

title: Sorting
text: sorted(iterable) returns a new sorted list; list.sort() sorts in place. Both accept key= and reverse=True: sorted(words, key=len), sorted(people, key=lambda p: (p.age, p.name)). Sorting is stable (Timsort).
